questions.question: In Belgium, what percentage of the total population lives in the Flemish region and speaks the Dutch language?
options: 59 percent
40 percent
80 percent
20 percent
questions.explanation: Of the country's total population, 59 percent lives in the Flemish region and speaks Dutch language. Another 40 percent people live in the Wallonia region and speak French. The remaining 1 percent of the Belgians speak German.

questions.question: In the capital city of Belgium, Brussels, what was the special linguistic composition that created tension?
options: 100% of the population spoke only German
80% people spoke French while 20% spoke Dutch, reversing the national majority
Dutch speakers were the overwhelming majority with 95% share
English was the sole mother tongue of all citizens
questions.explanation: In Brussels, 80 percent of the people speak French while 20 percent are Dutch-speaking. The Dutch-speaking people constituted a majority in the country, but a minority in the capital.

questions.question: In Sri Lanka, which social group forms the largest demographic majority of the population?
options: Tamil speakers (18%)
Christian community (7%)
Sinhala speakers (74%)
Muslim community (10%)
questions.explanation: The major social groups in Sri Lanka are the Sinhala-speakers (74 percent) and the Tamil-speakers (18 percent).

questions.question: Among Tamils in Sri Lanka, who are known as 'Indian Tamils'?
options: Tamil natives whose ancestors always lived in northern Sri Lanka
Merchants who migrated to Colombo after 1948
Diplomats posted at the Indian High Commission
Those whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers during the colonial period
questions.explanation: Tamil natives of the country are called 'Sri Lankan Tamils' (13 percent). The rest, whose forefathers came from India as plantation workers during colonial period, are called 'Indian Tamils' (5 percent).

questions.subtopic: Majoritarian Act of 1956 in Sri Lanka
questions.question: In 1956, an Act was passed by the Sri Lankan parliament to establish Sinhala supremacy. What did this Act mandate?
options: It introduced equal power sharing between Sinhalas and Tamils
It recognized Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil
It partitioned the island into two independent nations
It adopted English as the national language of Sri Lanka
questions.explanation: In 1956, an Act was passed to recognise Sinhala as the only official language, thus disregarding Tamil. The governments followed preferential policies that favoured Sinhala applicants for university positions and government jobs.

questions.subtopic: State Religion in Sri Lankan Constitution
questions.question: The new constitution of Sri Lanka stipulated that the state shall foster and protect which religion?
options: Hinduism
Christianity
Islam
Buddhism
questions.explanation: A new constitution stipulated that the state shall protect and foster Buddhism, further alienating the Sri Lankan Tamils who were predominantly Hindus and Muslims.

questions.question: By the 1980s, several political organisations were formed in Sri Lanka demanding which of the following?
options: Immediate merger of Sri Lanka with the Indian Union
Total ban on the Sinhala language in Colombo
An independent Tamil Eelam (state) in northern and eastern parts of Sri Lanka
Introduction of a military dictatorship
questions.explanation: By 1980s several political organisations were formed demanding an independent Tamil Eelam (state) in northern and eastern parts of Sri Lanka, leading to a prolonged civil war.

questions.question: Between 1970 and 1993, how many times did the leaders of Belgium amend their constitution to enable everyone to live together peacefully within the same country?
options: Four times
Two times
Ten times
Zero times
questions.explanation: Between 1970 and 1993, the Belgian leaders amended their constitution four times so as to work out an arrangement that would enable everyone to live together within the same country.

questions.question: Under the Belgian model of accommodation, what is the rule regarding the central government cabinet?
options: The number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers shall be equal in the central government
French ministers must hold at least 80% of all portfolios
The Prime Minister must always belong to the German minority
Ministers are chosen exclusively by the King without parliamentary vote
questions.explanation: Constitution prescribes that the number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers shall be equal in the central government. Some special laws require the support of majority of members from each linguistic group.

questions.question: Apart from the Central and State Governments, what unique third tier of government exists in Belgium?
options: Military tribunals headed by NATO generals
A religious clergy council representing Catholic bishops
Privatized corporate municipal councils
'Community Government' elected by people belonging to one language group (Dutch, French, and German)
questions.explanation: Apart from the Central and the State Government, there is a third kind of government. This 'community government' is elected by people belonging to one language community — Dutch, French and German-speaking — no matter where they live. It has power regarding cultural, educational and language-related issues.

questions.question: When many countries of Europe came together to form the European Union, which city was chosen as its headquarters due to its successful model of power sharing?
options: Paris
Brussels
Berlin
Geneva
questions.explanation: When many countries of Europe came together to form the European Union (EU), Brussels was chosen as its headquarters.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a 'prudential' reason for power sharing?
options: Power sharing is an intrinsic sacred moral virtue
It allows dictators to consolidate supreme personal power
It reduces the possibility of conflict between social groups and ensures political stability
It completely eliminates the need for periodic elections
questions.explanation: Prudential reasons stress that power sharing will bring out better outcomes. It helps to reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups, preventing violence and political instability.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a 'moral' reason for power sharing in a democracy?
options: Power sharing is the very spirit of democracy; people have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed
Power sharing maximizes industrial tax revenue for the state
It reduces administrative paper costs of government offices
It guarantees that only one political party remains in power forever
questions.explanation: Moral reasons emphasise the very act of power sharing as valuable. A democratic rule involves sharing power with those affected by its exercise, and who have to live with its effects.

questions.question: Power shared among different organs of government, such as the legislature, executive, and judiciary, is termed as:
options: Vertical division of power
Community power distribution
Federal delegation of power
Horizontal distribution of power
questions.explanation: Power is shared among different organs of government, such as the legislature, executive and judiciary. It is called horizontal distribution of power because it allows different organs of government placed at the same level to exercise different powers.

questions.question: Why is the horizontal distribution of power also known as a 'system of checks and balances'?
options: Banks check commercial loans and balance trade deficits
None of the organs can exercise unlimited power, and each organ checks the other, creating a balance of power
Citizens have to pay equal balance checks to judges and ministers
The military checks and balances the political parties
questions.explanation: In a horizontal arrangement, judges can check the functioning of executive or laws made by the legislatures. Even though ministers exercise power, they are responsible to the Parliament. This arrangement results in a system of checks and balances.

questions.question: Power shared among governments at different levels—such as a general central government for the entire country and provincial or regional governments—is called:
options: Horizontal distribution of power
Judicial supremacy
Vertical division of power
Bureaucratic delegation
questions.explanation: Division of power involving higher and lower levels of government (such as Union, State, and Local governments) is called vertical division of power.

questions.question: The system of 'reserved constituencies' in assemblies and the parliament of India is an example of power sharing among:
options: Different religious and socially weaker groups
Different multinational corporations
Armed forces and civilian police
The prime minister and the chief justice
questions.explanation: Power may also be shared among different social groups, such as the religious and linguistic groups. 'Community government' in Belgium and 'reserved constituencies' in India are good examples of this arrangement.

questions.question: When two or more political parties form an alliance to contest elections and win to form a government together, it is called a:
options: Unitary state
Coalition government
Presidential dictatorship
One-party regime
questions.explanation: When two or more parties form an alliance to contest elections, if their alliance is elected, they form a coalition government and thus share power directly.

questions.question: How do interest groups such as traders, businessmen, industrialists, farmers, and industrial workers share in governmental power?
options: By replacing the supreme court with trade union councils
By collecting national defense taxes directly from citizens
Through participation in governmental committees and bringing influence on decision-making processes
By appointing ambassadors to foreign countries
questions.explanation: Interest groups share governmental power either through participation in governmental committees or bringing influence on the decision-making process.

questions.question: What was the direct catastrophic consequence of majoritarian policies adopted by the Sri Lankan government?
options: Sri Lanka became the most prosperous nation in South Asia without poverty
Tamil was adopted as the universal language across all schools
The United Nations took over sovereign control of Sri Lanka
Distrust turned into widespread conflict and culminated in a protracted civil war
questions.explanation: The distrust between Sinhala and Tamil communities turned into widespread conflict and soon turned into a Civil War. As a result, thousands of people of both communities were killed, causing a terrible setback to the social, cultural and economic life of the country.
